title: Lyra and the Clock's Number Dance
markdown:
The Glimmerbrook clock tower was a dizzying mess! Its hands spun wildly, and a vital cog was gone. Builder Owen and inventor Dr. Hale were completely baffled. Oh, bother!

But Lyra, a moth with wings like shimmering rainbows, saw things others missed. While the men fretted, Lyra watched the clock hands. "Look!" she buzzed, her antennae twitching. When the big hand hit 12, the next number was 3. When it reached 6, the next was 9! "It's adding three every time!" she chirped. "A number dance!"

She fluttered to the worried men. "The numbers aren't lost!" she explained. "They always add three!"

Dr. Hale's eyes widened. "A pattern! Lyra, you clever moth, you've found its rhythm!"

Lyra's discovery was the key. Owen knew just what to make: a cog that kept the "add three" pattern going. He hammered and filed until a perfect new cog gleamed.

Up the tower Owen climbed. He fitted the cog. Whirr! Click! Tick-tock! The hands moved smoothly. The clock chimed, clear and true. Ding-dong!

"Hooray!" cheered Dr. Hale. "Lyra, you solved its secret dance!"

Lyra, who often felt too small, puffed out her chest. She, Lyra the moth, had fixed the village clock! It felt wonderful. "I wonder," she thought, her antennae buzzing, "what other amazing secrets the world is hiding?"
characters: Owen the patient builder, Lyra the moth, Dr. Hale
